d: It's always good to find a solid outdoor pool, especially in places like Avondale, Arizona. The Avondale pool has a reputation for being a good spot, that 4.6 rating from 57 reviews is pretty strong for a community pool. From what I hear, they've got some good stuff there for families. You've got your standard swimming area, but then a diving board too, which is always a hit. And for the really little ones, there's a separate kiddie pool. When it's time to eat, you don't have to pack a huge lunch; they have concessions and a picnic area. So, for a quick cool-off or a longer afternoon, it sounds like it covers the bases for different ages without being overly fancy. Plus, the adult admission is $12 and kids are $3, which is pretty standard. Avondale has about 90,000 people, so a good community spot makes sense.

It's always great to find a pool that doesn't charge admission, especially for kids. The Louisville Community Pool is one of those places. They've got an indoor setup, which means you can swim here all year, no matter the weather. That's a big plus in Louisville, a city with over 600,000 people. I've seen their Google rating is pretty solid, 4.4 stars from almost 270 reviews. They've also got some good amenities like a heated pool, a warm-up pool, and locker rooms, which are always handy. For families or even just someone looking for a free swim, this place seems like a good option. I get a lot of questions about free pools, and this one fits the bill.

It's an outdoor spot. Straight up, if you live in Decatur, Georgia (population 24,928 people, by the way), this is probably one of the main public options you're looking at. People seem to have mixed feelings, I've seen the Google rating is about a 3.5 out of 5 stars from close to 330 reviews. So, not everyone loves it, but it's getting used. You'll find things like lap lanes if you're looking to get some exercise, and they've got a diving board too, which is always a hit with kids. There's also a picnic area, which is pretty nice for hanging out after a swim. Admission is ten bucks for an adult, three for a kid. It's a pretty standard community pool experience from what I can tell. If you're okay with outdoor swimming and those prices work for you, it's worth checking out.

It sounds like The Bay Aquatic Center in Kansas City, MO is a pretty popular spot, judging by its 4.8 out of 5 stars from over 300 reviews. That's a solid rating for any pool. It's an outdoor kind of place, which means it's probably best for cooling off during the warmer months. They've got the basics covered, like restrooms and parking, which is important. Plus, with a picnic area and shade structures, you can make a whole afternoon of it, grab some food from the concessions, and stay out of the direct sun when you need a break. Being wheelchair accessible is a definite plus too. For a city like Kansas City, with a population of over half a million, having a good public pool like this is a real asset. I haven't been there myself, but the setup sounds good for a day of swimming.

When you're looking for a public pool in Fort Worth, the Tehama Ridge Swimming Pool is one option. It's got a solid 4 out of 5 stars from 10 Google reviews, which is decent. For a city of over 900,000 people, I'm always looking for pools that have good availability. This place seems to be open pretty consistently, from 6 AM to 9 PM every day of the week. That's a good chunk of time if you've got weird work hours or just like an early swim. It's located at 40967778, Fort Worth, TX 76177, so check that address on a map before you head out.

It looks like the YMCA of Greater San Francisco Association Office is more of an administrative hub than a spot to go for a swim. The hours listed, 9 AM to 5 PM, Monday through Friday, with weekends closed, really point to a business office. I mean, most pools are open early mornings and evenings, plus weekends, for people to actually use them. With only 11 reviews and a 4.2-star rating on Google, my guess is those reviews are about the Y's overall operations or maybe some other services, not specifically about a pool there. I'd definitely call them at (415) 777-9622 before heading over, especially if you're looking to swim. There are other YMCAs in San Francisco, so it might be worth checking their main website, ymcasf.org, for other locations with actual swimming facilities.

It looks like a pretty typical public pool in San Jose. For a city with over a million people, it's good to see facilities like these pop up. Finding a good public spot to swim can be tough sometimes, but this one's right there at 351 N 3rd St. When you're in a big city like San Jose, having accessible options is huge. I always tell people to check these kinds of city pools first, especially if you're not looking for anything fancy, just a clean place to get some laps in or cool off. It's definitely worth checking out if you're in that part of San Jose and need a swim. It's a solid choice for the community.

When I see a public pool with a 4.5-star rating from over 300 people, I pay attention. Big Stacy is in Austin, a city of almost a million people, so I expect it gets used a lot. It's listed at 700 E Live Oak St, and from what I dig up, it's open pretty early, 6 AM on weekdays. That's good for getting laps in before work. They close at 8 PM on weekdays too, so there's plenty of time. Weekends are a bit later, noon to 7 PM. I always recommend checking their site (austintexas.gov/department/big-stacy-pool) or just giving them a call at (512) 445-0304 if you're making a special trip. Things change, you know?

It's always good to see an honest-to-goodness outdoor pool, especially in a city like Memphis where the summers can get pretty hot. Frayser Park Pool is one of those spots. For me, when I think about a place like this, I picture families cooling off, and folks just enjoying the summer sun. It's a key part of the public infrastructure, really, helping a good chunk of the city's 633,104 people beat the heat. You can usually count on them for a refreshing swim when the weather's warm, and that's exactly what you'd want from an outdoor pool in Memphis. It's about access, and this provides it.

I've been looking at the Palms Pool in Las Vegas. It's a casino pool, so that tells you something about the vibe already. You're not going to be doing serious lap swimming here, that's for sure. It's open every day, 10 AM to 6 PM. Pretty consistent. With a Google rating of 3.7 out of 5 from 85 reviews, it's about what I'd expect for a place like this. It's probably good for hanging out, cooling off, maybe getting a drink. If you're staying at the Palms or are in that part of town, it could be a decent option for some casual recreation. Las Vegas has a population of over 640,000, and a good chunk of them are looking for a pool in the summer.

It's always a treat to find an outdoor pool, especially in a city the size of Aurora, Colorado. The Redstone Ranch Apartment Homes Pool sounds like a solid option if you're in that area. Aurora has well over 300,000 people, so having a more private-feeling pool can be a real plus. From what I know, it's exclusively one of those open-air setups, which makes it perfect for beating the summer heat. My guess is you'll find a mix of residents there, probably families and folks just looking to relax. It's not a huge public rec center, which means it probably won't be as chaotic. Sometimes, these apartment pools are a hidden gem if you know someone who lives there or if they offer day passes.

That Kiwanis place in Tempe, Arizona, is pretty well-regarded, 4.6 stars from 1700 reviews tells me it's a solid public pool option. It's open most days until 10 PM, except for Fridays through Sundays, so you've got a lot of flexibility there. For Tempe, a city of over 190,000, having a good public center like this is important. From what I see, it looks like a reliable spot whether you're looking to get some laps in after work or just cool off. I'd definitely check their site before heading out, given how much info is usually available for municipal pools. But yeah, if you're in that part of Arizona, it's worth checking out.
